title: BIPED: Pedagogically Informed Tutoring System for ESL Education
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to build conversational intelligent tutoring systems (CITS) for English as a second language that are not just fluent, but pedagogically meaningful. The authors argue that existing LLM-based tutoring systems often focus on simple concepts or limited dialogue strategies, and therefore do not capture the richer instructional tactics used by human tutors.

To address this, they construct BIPED, a bilingual tutoring dataset derived from one-on-one human ESL tutoring sessions. The dataset is annotated with a detailed dialogue-act taxonomy containing 34 tutor acts and 9 student acts, designed in collaboration with ESL instructors and refined through pilot sessions. They then use BIPED to build two tutoring-system implementations: one based on GPT-4 prompting and another based on instruction tuning of SOLAR-KO 10.7B. Both follow a two-step framework in which the model first predicts an appropriate tutor act and then generates the corresponding response.

The study uses 112 bilingual tutoring sessions with 4 experienced ESL tutors and 60 students. Sessions focused on reading and understanding a real news article, along with vocabulary, grammar, and cultural context. The paper reports that the fine-tuned model performs better than prompted GPT variants on tutor-act prediction and utterance generation metrics, and better reflects diverse pedagogical strategies. The main conclusion is that pedagogically structured data and act-conditioned generation can improve LLM-based tutoring for ESL, though the work remains primarily a static evaluation and does not yet include a full interactive human study.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical systems paper with a real tutoring dataset and pre/post tests, but it is not a randomized controlled trial or causal comparison of learning outcomes across conditions. The evaluation is primarily descriptive/offline model benchmarking plus a single-group learning-gain report, so causal credibility is limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported learning gain is modest (normalized gain=0.089), and the primary contributions are dataset and model-quality improvements rather than demonstrated large learner gains. The evidence suggests promise for ESL tutoring, but impact on broad educational outcomes remains unclear.

interventions.use_case: A bilingual conversational intelligent tutoring system for ESL education that uses GPT-4 prompting and fine-tuned SOLAR-KO to choose tutor dialogue acts and generate tutoring utterances for reading/vocabulary/grammar instruction.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that the tutoring sessions supported English proficiency gains and that the proposed LLM tutors produced human-like, pedagogically appropriate language. In the human tutoring dataset, the pre/post tutoring intervention yielded an average normalized learning gain of 0.089 (n=60 students; 112 sessions), and the fine-tuned model outperformed prompted GPT variants on utterance generation metrics including sBLEU=15.874 and BERTScore=0.716.
finding.measure: Pre/post English proficiency tests; generated utterance similarity to human tutor responses (sBLEU, BERTScore, embedding similarity); tutor act prediction accuracy

finding.finding_summary: The intervention was designed around reading an English news article with vocabulary and comprehension activities, and post-test items included reading comprehension, synonyms/antonyms, vocabulary, and phrasal verbs. The reported average normalized learning gain of 0.089 suggests modest improvement on literacy-related outcomes after tutoring, although the paper does not isolate which subskills improved most.
finding.measure: Reading comprehension, vocabulary, synonyms/antonyms, and phrasal verb pre/post-test scores
